_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Zimbabwe covering Great Zimbabwe, Mutapa Empire, Rozvi Confederacy, BSAC/Cecil Rhodes, Southern Rhodesia, UDI 1965, Bush War/liberation struggle, Mugabe era, hyperinflation, and Mnangagwa.

country_profile.government_type: Unitary presidential constitutional republic (de facto dominant-party)
country_profile.currency: Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG, introduced 2024) / US dollar (primary transactional currency)

religion.note: African Apostolic sects (white garments) are largest single denomination; syncretic Christianity/traditional practices common

ethnic_groups.name: Shona
ethnic_groups.notes: Bantu; dominant group; builders of Great Zimbabwe; major sub-groups: Karanga (south), Zezuru (central/Harare), Manyika (east), Korekore (north), Ndau (southeast), Rozwi; Mugabe was Zezuru; ZANU-PF heartland

ethnic_groups.name: Ndebele (Northern)
ethnic_groups.notes: Bantu (Nguni); Matabeleland; descended from Mzilikazi's Khumalo clan fleeing Shaka Zulu (1830s Mfecane); Bulawayo; ZAPU/MDC heartland; Gukurahundi massacres 1983-1987 targeted Ndebele

ethnic_groups.name: Tonga
ethnic_groups.notes: Binga/Lake Kariba; Bantu; displaced by Kariba Dam 1957-1958; marginalised; Zambezi Valley

ethnic_groups.name: Shangaan/Tsonga
ethnic_groups.notes: Southeast lowveld; Bantu; cross-border with Mozambique/South Africa; Gaza Empire heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Venda
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern border area; Bantu; cross-border with South Africa; Beitbridge

ethnic_groups.name: Kalanga
ethnic_groups.notes: Matabeleland South; Bantu; related to Shona; historically Torwa/Butua state; oldest Bantu group in Zimbabwe

ethnic_groups.name: White Zimbabwean
ethnic_groups.notes: British descent; formerly ~5% (1970s); most emigrated post-2000 land reform; farming, business; ~30,000 remaining

ethnic_groups.name: Asian (Indian/Chinese)
ethnic_groups.notes: Small Indian community; growing Chinese presence since 2000s

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Nambya, Chewa, Xhosa, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: Multiple smaller groups; 16 official languages reflect diversity

independence.notes: UDI by Ian Smith 1965 was unrecognised; Lancaster House Agreement 1979

country_profile.notes_unique: Named after Great Zimbabwe, the largest ancient stone structure in sub-Saharan Africa; experienced hyperinflation peaking at 79.6 billion percent in 2008; Victoria Falls is one of the Seven Natural Wonders.

natural_resources.notes: Africa's largest lithium reserves (Bikita, Arcadia mines — global EV demand driver); significant PGM deposits (Great Dyke); gold has long been major export; Marange diamond fields (controversial); tobacco is top agricultural export; fertile agricultural land (former 'breadbasket of Africa'); Victoria Falls tourism.

military.notes: Zimbabwe Defence Forces (ZDF); played role in 2017 coup removing Mugabe; deployed in DRC (SADC); liberation war background (ZANLA/ZIPRA); Gukurahundi massacres (1983-87, Matabeleland); military-business nexus (mining concessions); sanctioned officers.

infrastructure.notes: Econet, NetOne, Telecel telecoms; ZOL broadband; infrastructure deteriorating; landlocked (Beira, Maputo corridors).

debt_aid.notes: Chronic economic crisis; hyperinflation history ($100 trillion banknotes, 2008); new ZiG currency (Zimbabwe Gold, April 2024); arrears to World Bank/AfDB/IMF ($14B+ external debt); land reform legacy; US/EU sanctions (ZIDERA); lithium export ban (raw ore) to encourage domestic processing.

top_universities: National University of Science and Technology (NUST)
education.notes: One of Africa's highest literacy rates (Mugabe-era education investment); O-Level/A-Level British-style system; ZIMSEC examinations; brain drain has severely depleted teaching staff; school fees barrier in economic crisis; strong science/engineering tradition.

diaspora_migration.diaspora_population: 3 million+ (South Africa, UK, Botswana, Australia, Canada, USA, Mozambique, Namibia)
diaspora_migration.notes: Massive brain drain (~25% of population in diaspora); South Africa (~1.5M+ Zimbabweans, many undocumented); UK Zimbabwean community large (post-2000 exodus); Zimbabwean professionals (teachers, nurses, doctors) recruited worldwide; remittances ~10% GDP, essential for survival.
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: Brain drain crisis (3-5M in diaspora, mainly South Africa/UK); strict emigrant taxes

digital_economy.mobile_money_adoption: Very high (EcoCash dominant — 90%+ mobile money market, OneMoney, InnBucks)
digital_economy.notes: EcoCash (Cassava Smartech / Econet) processes ~$8B annually (~80% of Zimbabwe's transactions); mobile money effectively replaced banking for most citizens during currency crises; Econet Wireless (Strive Masiyiwa founded) dominant MNO; Zimbabwe silicon (Cassava, Sasai super-app); currency instability drives digital payment adoption.

country_profile.national_anthem: Blessed be the Land of Zimbabwe (Simudzai Mureza wedu WeZimbabwe)

lowest_point.name: Junction of Runde and Save Rivers

geography.terrain: Central plateau (highveld, 1200-1600m); Eastern Highlands (mountains); Zambezi Valley (north); Limpopo lowveld (south); middleveld (900-1200m)
major_lakes: Kariba (shared with Zambia, largest man-made by volume)
geography.notes: Victoria Falls (shared with Zambia, UNESCO); Great Zimbabwe ruins (UNESCO, namesake); Zimbabwe Bird symbol; landlocked; Matobo Hills (UNESCO, Cecil Rhodes grave); Lake Kariba.

economy_extended.notes: Multi-currency economy (USD dominant, ZiG gold-backed 2024); hyperinflation history (2008: 79.6 billion% monthly); mining (platinum #3 global, lithium Africa's largest, gold, chrome, diamonds); tobacco #1 export; sanctions; ZANU-PF dominance.

health.notes: HIV prevalence declining (from 25%+ to 11.6%); massive brain drain of health workers; cholera outbreaks (water infrastructure crisis); PEPFAR recipient; Parirenyatwa Hospital.

food_agriculture.notes: From 'breadbasket of Africa' to food insecurity (land reform 2000); tobacco #1 export; Command Agriculture programme; smallholder dominates; irrigation potential underutilized; El Niño drought 2024.

energy.notes: Kariba South Dam (1050 MW, shared); Hwange coal power station (expansion to 1520 MW); massive load shedding (18+ hours/day during drought); ZESA/ZETDC utility; solar growing; Batoka Gorge (planned).

transport.notes: NRZ (National Railways of Zimbabwe, deteriorated); road network degrading; Beitbridge border post (busiest in Southern Africa); landlocked (Beira/Maputo corridors to sea).

tourism.notes: 5 UNESCO sites; Victoria Falls; Great Zimbabwe (stone city, namesake); Hwange (largest NP); Mana Pools (canoe safaris); KAZA Transfrontier Area; potential untapped.

human_rights_gender.notes: ZANU-PF dominance since 1980; 2017 coup (Mugabe ousted); 2023 election disputed; opposition suppression (CCC, Citizens Coalition for Change); abduction/torture of activists; Patriotic Bill restricting dissent.

security_stability.notes: Politically repressive but not at war; Gukurahundi (1983-87, Matabeleland massacre, accountability sought); 2008 political violence; state-sponsored violence against opposition.

national_symbols: Zimbabwe Bird (soapstone raptor sculpture, from Great Zimbabwe)
major_festivals: Harare International Festival of the Arts (HIFA)
music_art_traditions: Mbira (thumb piano, Shona spiritual instrument, UNESCO potential)
intangible_heritage_items: Mbira playing and cultural practices (submitted to UNESCO)
notable_historical_figures: Robert Mugabe (1st PM/president, liberation hero turned autocrat)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: ZBC state (heavily controlled); NewsDay, Daily News (private); social media key for opposition; restricted press freedom
cultural_heritage.notes: Great Zimbabwe (stone civilization, 11th-15th century); Zimbabwe Bird (national identity); mbira spiritual music; stone sculpture world-renowned; Chimurenga (liberation war legacy).

legal_system.legal_tradition: English common law, Roman-Dutch law, customary law
legal_system.customary_law_role: Community courts; chiefs under Traditional Leaders Act; marriage/inheritance
legal_system.notes: 2013 constitution (referendum); Constitutional Court; BIPPA (Bilateral Investment Protection and Promotion Agreements); land reform (Fast Track, 2000+) ongoing legal disputes; Patriotic Bill (2023, anti-dissent).

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: 5 UNESCO sites; formerly 'breadbasket of Africa'; platinum/lithium rich.

current_leader.name: Emmerson Mnangagwa
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: ZANU-PF; 'The Crocodile'; CIO/intelligence background; 2017 coup against Mugabe; contested 2023 re-election; Western sanctions; Zimbabwe Gold currency introduced

former_leaders.name: Canaan Banana
former_leaders.notes: First president (ceremonial); ZANU; Methodist minister; later convicted of sexual offences

former_leaders.name: Robert Mugabe
former_leaders.notes: ZANU-PF; liberation hero turned dictator; Shona (Zezuru); teacher; Gukurahundi massacres (North Korean-trained 5th Brigade); land reform/Fast Track 2000 (seized white farms); hyperinflation ($100 trillion notes); economic collapse; ousted by military/Mnangagwa November 2017; died Singapore 2019

former_leaders.name: Abel Muzorewa
former_leaders.notes: UANC; first Black PM of Zimbabwe Rhodesia (short-lived internal settlement); rejected internationally
